captions.instagram:
What is combustion?

Burn a gas in a sealed jar on a balance and the reading doesn't budge: every atom is still there, just with new partners. Count them, weigh an LPG cylinder's 43 kg of CO₂, tune an engine's 14.7 : 1 mixture, put out a fire, and find out why lost fat leaves through your lungs.

→ Burn methane in a sealed jar and every atom just swaps partners. The balance does not move.
→ Open the jar and the fuel seems to vanish. Its gases float away, heavier than the fuel was.
→ Burn a 14.2 kg LPG cylinder and you make about 43 kg of CO₂, with oxygen taken from the air.
→ Steel wool gets heavier as it burns. The iron grabs oxygen: Lavoisier’s big clue.
→ A litre of petrol weighs 0.74 kg but makes 2.3 kg of CO₂. The rest is oxygen from 11 kg of air.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/combustionclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: What is combustion? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Burn a gas in a sealed jar on a balance and the reading doesn't budge: every atom is still there, just with new partners. Count them, weigh an LPG cylinder's 43 kg of CO₂, tune an engine's 14.7 : 1 mixture, put out a fire, and find out why lost fat leaves through your lungs.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/combustionclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/combustionclear

In this video:
• Burning swaps partners. A fuel made of carbon and hydrogen joins with oxygen.
• Gases weigh more than the fuel. The oxygen comes from the air, so the products outweigh the fuel.
• Air decides how clean it burns. Petrol needs 14.7 g of air per gram.
• Fire and your body. Take away fuel, heat or oxygen and a fire goes out.
• The limits. A candle only seems to vanish, because it is an open system.
